items.meaning: Used to confess something, often a feeling or opinion, that might be slightly surprising or reluctant.
items.example: I must admit, I was a little disappointed with the outcome of the project.
items.plain: I was a little disappointed with the outcome of the project.
items.note: Signals a slight reluctance to share a feeling, often a negative one, but can also be positive.

items.meaning: Describes a feeling of great comfort and reassurance after a period of worry or stress.
items.example: Hearing that the flight wasn't cancelled was a huge relief, as I really needed to get home.
items.plain: Hearing that the flight wasn't cancelled made me feel much better, as I really needed to get home.
items.note: Commonly used to express strong positive feelings after a negative situation is avoided.

items.meaning: Expresses sympathy by acknowledging the difficulty of someone's experience, even if you haven't lived it.
items.example: You've been through so much lately; I can only imagine how exhausted you must feel.
items.plain: You've been through so much lately; I understand you must feel very exhausted.
items.note: An empathetic phrase, used to show understanding and support for someone's difficult situation.

items.meaning: Expresses genuine happiness and satisfaction upon receiving good news or information.
items.example: I'm so pleased to hear that your project was approved; you've put in a lot of effort.
items.plain: I'm very happy that your project was approved; you've put in a lot of effort.
items.note: A warm and sincere way to react positively to someone's good news or success.

items.meaning: Expresses mild disappointment or sympathy for an unfortunate situation.
items.example: Oh, that's a shame you can't make it to the dinner party after all.
items.plain: Oh, it's disappointing you can't make it to the dinner party after all.
items.note: A common, gentle way to express regret or mild sadness about something.

items.meaning: Indicates that a situation is less than perfect or causes some inconvenience, without being overly negative.
items.example: Having to work late again is not ideal, but we need to meet the deadline.
items.plain: Having to work late again is inconvenient, but we need to meet the deadline.
items.note: A polite and understated way to express mild annoyance or dissatisfaction.

items.meaning: Describes something truly unexpected or astonishing.
items.example: Her promotion was a genuine surprise to everyone, as she'd only been there a year.
items.plain: Her promotion was truly unexpected to everyone, as she'd only been there a year.
items.note: Used to convey authentic surprise, often when something positive or unexpected happens.

items.meaning: Indicates understanding and agreement with an explanation or a point of view.
items.example: Ah, that makes sense now why the system was behaving so strangely.
items.plain: Ah, I understand now why the system was behaving so strangely.
items.note: A common phrase to acknowledge clarity and logical understanding.

items.meaning: Expresses complete understanding and empathy for someone's feelings or situation.
items.example: I totally get it; it's frustrating when your hard work isn't recognized.
items.plain: I completely understand; it's frustrating when your hard work isn't recognized.
items.note: An informal but widely used phrase to show strong empathy and comprehension.

items.meaning: Expresses gratitude or acknowledgement for someone's effort, understanding, or offer.
items.example: I appreciate that you stayed late to help me finish the report.
items.plain: I'm grateful that you stayed late to help me finish the report.
items.note: A polite and common way to show thanks or acknowledge a helpful gesture.

items.meaning: Expresses satisfaction or relief upon learning new information, often positive or reassuring.
items.example: I'm glad to know that the project is back on track after all the delays.
items.plain: I'm happy that the project is back on track after all the delays.
items.note: Used to convey positive feelings about receiving information that resolves uncertainty.

items.meaning: Expresses mild surprise or shock, often implying a slight feeling of being unsettled or confused.
items.example: I'm a bit taken aback by their sudden decision to change the entire strategy.
items.plain: I'm slightly surprised by their sudden decision to change the entire strategy.
items.note: Suggests a reaction of unexpectedness that leaves one momentarily speechless or disoriented.

items.meaning: Describes a complex or difficult circumstance that requires careful handling or thought.
items.example: It's a tricky situation, and I'm not sure what the best course of action is.
items.plain: It's a difficult situation, and I'm not sure what the best course of action is.
items.note: A common way to acknowledge complexity and express a need for careful consideration.

items.meaning: Expresses surprise or disbelief about something, implying it goes against one's expectations.
items.example: I wouldn't have thought he'd be interested in that kind of research.
items.plain: I didn't expect him to be interested in that kind of research.
items.note: Used to convey mild surprise or to indicate that something was unexpected.

items.meaning: Expresses sincere gratitude and appreciation for someone's thoughtful gesture or offer.
items.example: That's really kind of you to offer to help me move house this weekend.
items.plain: It's very thoughtful of you to offer to help me move house this weekend.
items.note: A warm and polite way to thank someone for their generosity or helpfulness.

items.meaning: Describes a feeling of sadness or dissatisfaction when expectations are not met.
items.example: There was a sense of disappointment when the project deadline was extended again.
items.plain: People felt sad when the project deadline was extended again.
items.note: A common way to describe a general feeling of dissatisfaction or regret.

items.meaning: Introduces a piece of good news or a positive outcome that alleviates previous worry.
items.example: I'm relieved to say that the test results came back negative.
items.plain: I'm happy to say that the test results came back negative.
items.note: Used to share reassuring news, often after a period of anxiety.

items.meaning: Expresses hesitation or uncertainty, often used as a softener before stating a potential problem or lack of knowledge.
items.example: I'm not entirely sure that's the best approach for this particular problem.
items.plain: I'm uncertain if that's the best approach for this particular problem.
items.note: A polite way to express doubt or to gently disagree without being confrontational.

items.meaning: Used to introduce unwelcome or bad news, softening the impact by expressing reluctance to deliver it.
items.example: I'm afraid to say we've run into a few unexpected issues with the budget.
items.plain: Unfortunately, we've run into a few unexpected issues with the budget.
items.note: A common and polite way to deliver negative information.

items.meaning: Describes a situation that causes mild annoyance or irritation due to obstacles or lack of progress.
items.example: It's a bit frustrating when you put in so much effort and don't see immediate results.
items.plain: It's slightly annoying when you put in so much effort and don't see immediate results.
items.note: A common and understated way to express mild irritation or impatience.

items.meaning: Acknowledges understanding of someone else's perspective, even if you don't fully agree.
items.example: I can see your point about the workload, but we still need to prioritize this task.
items.plain: I understand your perspective about the workload, but we still need to prioritize this task.
items.note: A diplomatic phrase used to show understanding in a discussion or disagreement.

items.meaning: Expresses a genuine and heartfelt apology for a mistake or an unfortunate event.
items.example: Please accept my sincere apologies for the misunderstanding earlier.
items.plain: Please accept my true apologies for the misunderstanding earlier.
items.note: A more formal and emphatic way to apologize than 'I'm sorry'.

items.meaning: Expresses strong positive reaction and delight upon hearing very good information.
items.example: Oh, that's wonderful news! I knew you'd do great on your presentation.
items.plain: Oh, that's very good news! I knew you'd do great on your presentation.
items.note: A common and enthusiastic way to react to positive developments.

items.meaning: Describes a feeling of extreme happiness and joy about a particular event or outcome.
items.example: Winning the award brought her absolute delight after years of hard work.
items.plain: Winning the award made her extremely happy after years of hard work.
items.note: A strong expression of joy, often used for significant positive events.

items.meaning: Expresses mild worry or apprehension about a situation or potential outcome.
items.example: I'm a little concerned about the new changes to the company policy.
items.plain: I'm slightly worried about the new changes to the company policy.
items.note: A polite and common way to voice a moderate level of worry or unease.

items.meaning: Expresses a moderate level of astonishment or unexpectedness regarding something.
items.example: I'm quite surprised by how quickly they adapted to the new software.
items.plain: I'm rather astonished by how quickly they adapted to the new software.
items.note: Used to convey a genuine, but not overwhelming, sense of surprise.

items.text: I was under the impression that
items.form: I was under the impression that
items.meaning: Used to express mild surprise or confusion when a belief turns out to be incorrect.
items.example: I was under the impression that the meeting was scheduled for Tuesday, not Wednesday.
items.plain: I thought the meeting was scheduled for Tuesday, not Wednesday.
items.note: A polite way to correct a misunderstanding or express mild annoyance at a change.

items.meaning: Describes something that causes a slight degree of anxiety or apprehension.
items.example: The unexpected delay in the shipment is a bit of a worry for our production schedule.
items.plain: The unexpected delay in the shipment is slightly concerning for our production schedule.
items.note: A common and understated way to express mild concern.

items.meaning: Expresses genuine regret or sadness about an unfortunate situation or missed opportunity.
items.example: It's a real pity that they had to cancel the annual conference this year.
items.plain: It's truly regrettable that they had to cancel the annual conference this year.
items.note: A common phrase to express sincere regret or disappointment.

items.meaning: Expresses an unavoidable or strong personal emotion or opinion about a situation.
items.example: I can't help but feel a little sad that the project is finally over.
items.plain: I feel a little sad that the project is finally over, and I can't avoid it.
items.note: Used to convey a strong, often persistent, emotional reaction or intuition.

items.meaning: Expresses a moderate level of satisfaction or contentment regarding an outcome or situation.
items.example: I'm quite pleased with how the team handled the unexpected challenges.
items.plain: I'm rather satisfied with how the team handled the unexpected challenges.
items.note: A polite and common way to express positive evaluation or contentment.

items.text: I'm not sure what to say
items.form: I'm not sure what to say
items.meaning: Expresses a feeling of being overwhelmed, surprised, or at a loss for words, often in response to unexpected news.
items.example: When they told me I got the scholarship, I was so shocked, I'm not sure what to say.
items.plain: When they told me I got the scholarship, I was so shocked, I didn't know how to react.
items.note: Used to convey a strong emotional reaction that leaves one speechless.

items.meaning: Expresses a strong positive impression, admiration, or liking for something or someone.
items.example: I'm quite taken with the new design of the office space; it's very modern.
items.plain: I'm rather impressed by the new design of the office space; it's very modern.
items.note: A slightly more formal way to express strong positive feelings or admiration.

items.text: a feeling of being put out
items.form: a feeling of being put out
items.meaning: Describes mild annoyance or irritation, often because of an inconvenience or slight.
items.example: I had a feeling of being put out when they changed the schedule without telling me.
items.plain: I felt slightly annoyed when they changed the schedule without telling me.
items.note: A common, understated way to express mild irritation or feeling inconvenienced.

items.meaning: Expresses eager anticipation and positive expectation for a future event.
items.example: I'm quite looking forward to the company retreat next month.
items.plain: I'm really anticipating the company retreat next month.
items.note: A common and polite way to express excitement about a future event.

items.meaning: Expresses strong relief or happiness about a positive outcome or avoided negative situation.
items.example: I'm just so glad that everyone arrived safely despite the bad weather.
items.plain: I'm very relieved that everyone arrived safely despite the bad weather.
items.note: A warm and sincere way to express strong positive feelings, often relief.

items.meaning: Expresses a feeling of emotional warmth, gratitude, or sympathy in response to someone's kindness or story.
items.example: I'm quite touched by your thoughtful gesture of bringing me flowers.
items.plain: I'm rather moved by your thoughtful gesture of bringing me flowers.
items.note: Used to convey a sincere emotional reaction to kindness or a moving story.

items.text: I'm not sure how to feel
items.form: I'm not sure how to feel
items.meaning: Expresses confusion or mixed emotions in response to complex or unexpected news.
items.example: After hearing both sides of the story, I'm not sure how to feel about the situation.
items.plain: After hearing both sides of the story, I have mixed emotions about the situation.
items.note: A common phrase to convey uncertainty or conflicting emotions.

items.meaning: Expresses genuine sympathy or regret about someone's bad news or difficult situation.
items.example: Oh, I'm so sorry to hear about your grandmother's illness; please let me know if there's anything I can do.
items.plain: Oh, I feel bad about your grandmother's illness; please let me know if there's anything I can do.
items.note: A common, heartfelt expression of sympathy. Use for serious or moderately serious bad news.

items.example: Losing your job and then having car trouble, that's really tough, I hope things improve soon.
items.plain: Losing your job and then having car trouble, that's very difficult, I hope things improve soon.
items.note: Informal and empathetic. Shows understanding of another's hardship.

items.example: I can't imagine how stressful it must be to manage two young children and a full-time job.
items.plain: I don't know how stressful it must be to manage two young children and a full-time job.
items.note: A strong expression of empathy, often used when someone is describing a challenging situation.

items.meaning: Expresses sudden comfort or reassurance after a period of worry or anxiety.
items.example: The test results came back negative? Oh, what a relief! I was so worried for you.
items.plain: The test results came back negative? Oh, I feel so much better! I was so worried for you.
items.note: A very common, natural exclamation of relief. Can be used for small or large worries.

items.meaning: Expresses great happiness and excitement for someone else's good fortune or success.
items.example: You got the promotion you wanted? I'm thrilled for you, you really deserve it!
items.plain: You got the promotion you wanted? I'm very happy for you, you really deserve it!
items.note: A warm and enthusiastic way to share in someone's joy. More intense than

items.plain: Oh, I regret hearing that; your flight was cancelled, which is really inconvenient.
items.note: A common, polite way to express sympathy for minor inconveniences or bad news.

items.meaning: Expresses mild disappointment or sympathy for a minor negative event.
items.example: You missed the deadline? Oh, that's too bad, but I'm sure you'll do better next time.
items.plain: You missed the deadline? Oh, that's disappointing, but I'm sure you'll do better next time.
items.note: Casual and empathetic, suitable for everyday conversations among friends or colleagues.

items.meaning: Expresses mild annoyance or frustration about something bothersome.
items.example: The printer's jammed again? What a nuisance, especially when I'm in a hurry.
items.plain: The printer's jammed again? That's annoying, especially when I'm in a hurry.
items.note: Used for minor, irritating problems; can be said to oneself or others.

items.meaning: Expresses strong happiness and pleasure for someone else's good fortune.
items.example: You got the promotion? That's fantastic! I'm delighted for you and your hard work.
items.plain: You got the promotion? That's fantastic! I'm very happy for you and your hard work.
items.note: A warm and sincere expression of joy for another person's success.

items.meaning: Expresses strong happiness and pleasure for someone else's good news or success.
items.example: Your daughter got into her dream university? I'm so happy for you all!
items.plain: Your daughter got into her dream university? I'm very pleased for you all!
items.note: A very common and heartfelt way to share in someone's joy.

items.meaning: Expresses deep regret or apology for something that has happened.
items.example: I'm truly sorry that your project didn't get the funding it deserved this year.
items.plain: I deeply regret that your project didn't get the funding it deserved this year.
items.note: More emphatic than "I'm sorry," conveying deeper regret or sympathy.

items.meaning: Expresses understanding and shared experience with someone's feelings or situation.
items.example: Dealing with endless paperwork is exhausting; I can relate to that completely.
items.plain: Dealing with endless paperwork is exhausting; I understand that feeling completely.
items.note: Shows empathy by indicating you've had a similar experience or feeling.

items.meaning: Expresses sympathy and understanding for a difficult situation someone is facing.
items.example: Losing your pet after so many years, that must be tough to go through.
items.plain: Losing your pet after so many years, that must be difficult to go through.
items.note: A compassionate way to acknowledge someone's hardship without being intrusive.

items.meaning: Expresses sincere astonishment at something unexpected.
items.example: I'm genuinely surprised by how quickly they managed to resolve the issue.
items.plain: I'm truly astonished by how quickly they managed to resolve the issue.
items.note: Emphasizes the sincerity of the surprise, often positive or neutral.

items.meaning: Expresses a moderate level of unhappiness or dissatisfaction.
items.example: I'm rather disappointed that the event was cancelled at the last minute.
items.plain: I'm somewhat unhappy that the event was cancelled at the last minute.
items.note: A polite and slightly formal way to express dissatisfaction.

items.meaning: Expresses extreme excitement and happiness.
items.example: I'm absolutely thrilled that our team won the championship this year!
items.plain: I'm extremely excited that our team won the championship this year!
items.note: Conveys intense joy and enthusiasm, often for significant positive news.

items.meaning: Expresses great comfort and ease after a period of worry or stress.
items.example: The test results came back negative, and I'm so relieved to hear that.
items.plain: The test results came back negative, and I feel great comfort to hear that.
items.note: A common and natural expression of relief, often after a scare.

items.meaning: Expresses sincere appreciation and thankfulness.
items.example: For all your help with the move, I'm truly grateful; I couldn't have done it alone.
items.plain: For all your help with the move, I'm sincerely thankful; I couldn't have done it alone.
items.note: A more formal and emphatic way to express thanks than "thank you."

items.plain: I'm profoundly unhappy to learn of your grandmother's passing; she was a wonderful woman.
items.note: Used for serious, often tragic, news; conveys strong empathy.

items.meaning: Expresses a moderate level of worry or anxiety about a situation.

items.meaning: Expresses moderate satisfaction or happiness.

items.plain: I'm moderately satisfied with the outcome of the negotiations, all things considered.

items.plain: I'm extremely happy that you'll be joining our team next month.

items.meaning: Expresses a state of moderate happiness and satisfaction regarding something specific.

items.note: A polite way to introduce an unwelcome request or task.

items.note: A formal and polite apology for disruption, often in professional settings.

items.meaning: Expresses mild annoyance or inconvenience, often feeling slightly offended by something.

items.meaning: Expresses extreme happiness and excitement about a future possibility.

items.note: Conveys strong enthusiasm for a future opportunity or event.

items.plain: I'm moderately comforted to hear that your surgery went well and you're recovering.
items.note: A common and natural expression of relief for less intense situations.

items.meaning: Expresses a moderate belief that good things will happen regarding something specific.

items.text: I'm rather concerned about the implications
items.form: I'm rather concerned about the implications
items.meaning: Expresses moderate worry about the potential consequences of something.
items.example: I'm rather concerned about the implications of this new policy on our long-term strategy.
items.plain: I'm somewhat worried about the consequences of this new policy on our long-term strategy.
items.note: A formal way to express worry about future effects, often in professional contexts.

items.meaning: Expresses extreme happiness and excitement about being in a certain state or role.
items.example: I'm absolutely thrilled to be part of such a dedicated and innovative team.

items.note: Conveys intense joy about one's current position or involvement.

items.text: I'm so sorry to bother you
items.form: I'm so sorry to bother you
items.meaning: Expresses polite regret before interrupting or making a request.

items.plain: I regret interrupting you, but could you spare a moment to look at this?
items.note: A common and polite softener when initiating an interaction or request.

items.text: I'm quite taken with the notion
items.form: I'm quite taken with the notion
items.meaning: Expresses a strong positive impression or attraction to a specific thought or belief.

items.note: Indicates a strong liking or interest in a particular belief or abstract idea.

items.note: A polite and formal apology for potential or actual problems.

items.text: I'm quite put out by the fact that
items.form: I'm quite put out by the fact that

items.note: A common and natural expression of relief for a specific positive outcome.
